_exemplar: GOLD EXAMPLE, review-report (tier 2, approved). Constructed teaching exemplar: the Tyro run predates the tiered judge protocol, so no real tier-2 report exists. This reconstructs the final peer pass a second judge would have run at step_audit after the seven review rounds, judging the same approved v2 the tier-1 exemplar covers. Quotes are verbatim from examples/cover-letter-gold.md. The teaching point: this report runs at step_audit, but its rules_audit is scoped to the judged artifact's step (step_4, which the gate derives from artifact: cover-letter-draft-v2.md), not to step_audit. That is the fix for the vacuous tier-2 audit: an empty rules_audit at step_audit fails the gate; the peer judge re-audits the letter's quote and measure rules with quotes verified against v2. Zero flagged items is the normal shape for a clean final pass. A real report's judge.identity names the model or agent that actually judged; the gate refuses template placeholders, so this constructed exemplar marks itself instead. Remove this _exemplar key when copying the schema.

notes: Constructed exemplar (tier 2, approved). The peer judge consumed the accumulated tier-1 reports (review-report-step_3.json, review-report-step_4.json), re-audited the letter's step_4 rules independently, and confirmed the delta. Zero flagged items: a clean final pass adds no flags. Contested tier-2 findings follow the capped re-judge protocol (2 rounds), then escalate to the human checkpoint. Same artifact as the tier-1 exemplar, deliberately: the value of tier 2 is a second, independent verdict on the same mechanical claims, and the gate re-verifies this report's quotes against v2 exactly as it did for tier 1.
